fact.value: 2-L oven-dried four-necked round-bottomed flask with mechanical stirrer, 30-cm reflux condenser open to air, two septa, and thermocouple
CuI, paraformaldehyde, and THF were charged and mechanical stirring was initiated
diisopropylamine was added in one portion by graduated cylinder, followed by propargyl alcohol by syringe; rapid stirring was required because the mixture became thick/sticky
open to air; no inert-atmosphere protection
heated to THF reflux in a heating mantle; the orange mixture slowly became reddish-brown
allowed to cool to room temperature
transferred to a 3-L flask and concentrated by rotary evaporation
the original 2-L flask was charged with a cold diethyl ether/12 N HCl solution and agitated
the concentrated reaction solution was poured into the cold acidic mixture in five portions approximately 3 min apart
agitation was stopped; the yellow supernatant was decanted onto a short silica-gel column and vacuum was applied briefly
height 3.0 cm, diameter 6.5 cm; silica gel 10–40 um

residue was extracted with 100 mL diethyl ether, stirred 3 min, settled 3 min, decanted, and filtered through the same silica pad; this extraction/settling/decantation/filtration cycle was performed three times total
wash filtrate with saturated NaCl (2 × 100 mL); combine aqueous phases and back-extract with diethyl ether (2 × 100 mL); combine organic phases, dry over anhydrous sodium sulfate, and filter
concentrated by rotary evaporation, transferred to a 250-mL flask with approximately 50 mL MTBE, and further concentrated in vacuo
short-path distillation was initiated with a 10-mL receiver chilled to −78 °C; a forerun was collected and the distillation temperature then dropped
receiver changed to a 25-mL flask chilled to −78 °C and distillation restarted; the main colorless fraction was collected
isolated main fraction after short-path distillation
500 MHz 1H NMR analysis using dimethyl fumarate as the internal standard
colorless immediately after distillation, slowly becoming light yellow

notes.value: Pages 1–6 are one continuous large-scale preparation and workup; reaction photographs Figures 1–4 document appearance/filtration and do not define additional experiments.

GC conditions: DB-1701 column (30 m × 250 um, film 0.15 um), flow 1.2 mL/min, injector 240 °C, 50→150 °C at 15 °C/min, 150→280 °C at 20 °C/min, hold 280 °C for 2 min, FID 280 °C; retention times 2.18 min for propargyl alcohol and 2.55 min for product.

CuI is retained conservatively as a reagent rather than auto-assigned a catalyst role; its source-reported loading is already structured in participant amounts, and the covered procedure does not call it a catalyst.

Note 10 warns that the pungent reddish-brown residue can clog the filter and instructs decanting only liquid.
Page 7 supplies the source spectra: 1H NMR, 13C NMR, EI-MS, and neat IR for buta-2,3-dien-1-ol; these characterize the existing preparation rather than creating another reaction.

The page-9 discussion summarizes the current 0.4 mol procedure as giving 38–45% product with the source-reported CuI charge already structured in participant amounts; this is a narrative range for the same method, not another run or a replacement for the run-specific 45% outcome.
